title: Intrusion Prevention
desc: fail2ban-style protection: finds malicious IPs through log jails, trap ports and port-scan detection, bans them and syncs the bans to the system firewall (nftables / iptables + ipset)

fw.title: System firewall
fw.rulesTitle: Rules Gately wrote to nftables (table inet gately)
fw.rulesTitleIpt: Rules Gately wrote to iptables (GATELY_* chains in the mangle table and ipset sets)
fw.disabledHint: Bans only apply to Gately's own services (port forwarding, web service, STUN, WebDAV, FTP, SMB and the admin console). Trap ports are served by Gately itself and port-scan detection is unavailable. Turn it on under Settings.
fw.hintOS: Firewall sync is Linux only. Bans still apply to Gately's own services, trap ports are served by Gately itself and port-scan detection is unavailable.
fw.reasonUnsupported: The system kernel does not support nftables
fw.hintUnsupported: The kernel does not have nf_tables enabled (Synology DSM, for example) and no usable iptables (legacy) and ipset were found, so retries have stopped. With Docker, update to the latest image (it includes iptables-legacy and ipset); for a direct install, install ipset and iptables (the legacy variant), then save once under Settings. Until then bans still apply to Gately's own services (port forwarding, web service, STUN, WebDAV, FTP, SMB and the admin console), trap ports are served by Gately itself and port-scan detection is unavailable.
fw.reasonMissing: The nft command was not found
fw.hintMissing: Install nftables (Debian / Ubuntu: apt install nftables; OpenWrt 22.03 and later ship it). Save the settings once after installing.
fw.hintMissingDocker: This image does not include nft. Update to the latest image.
fw.reasonPermission: No permission to change the firewall
fw.hintPermission: Writing to nftables requires root or CAP_NET_ADMIN. For a systemd service add AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_ADMIN CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE under [Service].
fw.hintPermissionDocker: Add cap_add: [NET_ADMIN] to docker-compose.yml, use network_mode: host and recreate the container.
fw.hintError: The kernel may be missing nftables modules (nf_tables, nft_set_hash and so on), or nft is too old (0.9.0 or later is required). Details below.

sourceHelp.file: Follows new lines appended to the file and switches to the new file after rotation. One path per line.
sourceHelp.fileDocker: Gately runs in a container and can only read files mounted into it. For example, mount the host's /var/log read-only at /var/log/host inside the container and enter /var/log/host/auth.log.
sourceHelp.journal: Reads the service's log through journalctl. One unit per line, e.g. ssh.service.
sourceHelp.journalMissing: journalctl was not found (in a container or on a system without systemd), so this source is unavailable.
sourceHelp.command: Runs a command that keeps printing log lines and reads its output, e.g. logread -f on OpenWrt. The command is restarted when it exits.
sourceHelp.docker: Reads the container's log. The Docker module must be able to reach Docker.
sourceHelp.event: Counts Gately's own events, which carry the source IP. No filter is needed.
sourceHelp.web: Counts requests handled by the Web service by listener, path and status code, without reading any log. Whichever listener triggers it, the ban applies to all sites and the system firewall.
sourceHelp.tls: Counts TLS handshake failures on the Web service HTTPS listeners by failure type, listener and number of times. Probes that drop during the handshake never send an HTTP request, so path probing cannot see them. A ban applies to all sites and the system firewall.

jail.intro: Finds failures in logs. An IP that reaches the count within the time window is banned.
jail.empty: No jails yet. Add common services such as SSH, Nginx or Vaultwarden from a template.
jail.deleteConfirm: Delete this jail? Existing bans stay until they expire.
jail.filterHelp: Go regular expressions, one per line. <HOST> stands for the source IP (IPv4 and IPv6). Each line matching any filter counts as one failure.
jail.ignoreHelp: Optional regular expressions, one per line. Matching lines are not counted.
jail.testPlaceholder: Paste a few log lines to check that the filters extract the IP
jail.listenersHelp: Leave empty for all listeners. Whichever listener triggers it, the ban applies to all sites and the system firewall.
jail.pathsHelp: One per line; leave empty for all paths. * matches any characters (including /), the whole path must match, case-insensitive. For example */.env matches /.env and /api/.env. Lines starting with ~ are Go regular expressions.
jail.ignorePathsHelp: Optional, same syntax as Paths. Matching requests are not counted.
jail.anyStatusHelp: When off, only 404 and 444 (missing content or closed connection) are counted, so regular visitors and users sharing an outbound IP are not banned by mistake. Decoy paths are never visited by regular users, so it can be turned on there: single-page apps return 200 for any path.
jail.unknownHostHelp: Counts only requests whose domain matches no site, that is, requests handled by the default site or answered with 404.
jail.testPathsPlaceholder: One path per line, such as /.env. Only the path rules are tested
jail.tlsKindsHelp: Tick the failure types to count, at least one. Browser preconnects and phone network switches also cause "dropped mid-handshake", so set a generous count for those.
jail.testReasonsPlaceholder: One handshake failure reason per line, e.g. EOF or tls: first record does not look like a TLS handshake; only the type is tested

trap.title: Trap ports
trap.help: Sets traps on ports this host does not use. Any source that connects to them is banned. Normal users never touch these ports, so this catches mass scanning well. Ports that are listening are excluded automatically.
trap.portsHelp: Comma separated, ranges allowed, e.g. 23,3389,5900-5910. LAN and whitelisted addresses never trigger them.
trap.userspace: Firewall not active, Gately listens on: {ports} (only catches scans that complete the handshake)
trap.skipped: These ports are in use and were excluded: {ports}

scan.title: Port-scan detection
scan.help: Counts how often each source connects to ports that are not open on this host and bans it when it exceeds the threshold per minute. Only new connections to this host count; traffic forwarded to containers or LAN devices is ignored.
scan.needFirewall: Kernel-side trap ports and port-scan detection both require firewall sync to be active. See the status above.
scan.thresholdHelp: A source is banned when it connects to closed ports more often than this per minute. A normal client retrying a closed port does so about 5 times a minute, so keep this at 10 or above.
scan.excludeHelp: {count} ports are listening and count as open automatically. Add ports used by other programs through firewall rules here.
scan.ipv6StrictHelp: When on, IPv6 sources may only connect to open ports (listening ports plus the extra open ports above); the first connection to any other port gets them banned, with no threshold counting. IPv4 still uses the threshold. Bans apply to the whole /64, so other devices in the same /64 are banned too; whitelisted addresses are not affected. A port that starts listening counts as open within about 10 seconds, and the mode takes effect about 15 seconds after being turned on or after a restart. Ports used by other programs through firewall rules must be added to the extra open ports first, or visitors using them will be banned. TCP only. When using the FTP service, set a passive port range; the whole range counts as open automatically.

settings.firewallHelp: Creates the inet gately table in nftables and drops all traffic from banned addresses in the kernel, including traffic forwarded to Docker containers and LAN devices. Replies to connections this host opens to those addresses (DNS, package mirrors and so on) still get through. The rules are removed when this is turned off or Gately stops. When the kernel has no nf_tables (Synology DSM, for example), the mangle table of iptables (legacy) and ipset sets are used instead, with the same effect.
settings.firewallUnsupported: The system kernel does not support nftables, so this has no effect and can be turned off.
settings.incrementHelp: When an address is banned again within 30 days, the duration doubles each time.
settings.ignorePrivateHelp: Loopback, private addresses, 100.64.0.0/10 (carrier-grade NAT and Tailscale), link-local addresses and the IPv6 /64 networks of this host's interfaces are never banned automatically, and trap ports and scan detection ignore them.
settings.ignoreListHelp: One IP or CIDR network per line. These are never banned automatically; manual bans ignore the whitelist.

sshd-journal.name: SSH (systemd journal)
sshd-journal.desc: Reads the log of ssh.service / sshd.service

dropbear.name: Dropbear (OpenWrt)
dropbear.desc: Reads OpenWrt SSH login failures through logread -f

nginx-http-auth.name: Nginx basic auth
nginx-http-auth.desc: Wrong user names or passwords in error.log

nginx-botsearch.name: Nginx bot search
nginx-botsearch.desc: Requests in access.log probing wp-login, .env, phpMyAdmin and similar paths

vaultwarden.name: Vaultwarden
vaultwarden.desc: Login and two-step failures in the vaultwarden container

homeassistant.name: Home Assistant
homeassistant.desc: Login failures in the homeassistant container (http logging must be on)

gately-admin.name: Gately admin login
gately-admin.desc: Failed admin console logins (password, two-step code, passkey)

gately-waf.name: WAF blocks
gately-waf.desc: Sources blocked by the WAF repeatedly. Do not use it for sites behind a CDN that passes the real IP in a header, or the CDN's nodes get banned

gately-knock.name: Failed port knocks
gately-knock.desc: Sources that repeatedly send knock packets that fail authentication, are replayed or request unauthorized ports (counted at most once every 5 seconds per source)

web-decoy.name: Web decoy paths
web-decoy.desc: Bans on the first request to paths scanners love, such as /.env, /.git and wp-login.php, whatever the status code. Remove matching lines first if a site actually runs WordPress, phpMyAdmin and the like

web-unknown-host.name: Unknown domain scans
web-unknown-host.desc: Bans after 5 requests within 1 minute by IP or by a domain with no site (handled by the default site or answered with 404)

web-404.name: Web 404 probing
web-404.desc: Bans after 10 requests for missing paths (404 or 444) within 1 minute; common paths such as favicon and robots.txt are excluded

tls-probe.name: TLS abnormal handshake
tls-probe.desc: Sources sending plain HTTP, a too-old protocol version or unnegotiable parameters are banned after 5 times in 1 minute. Normal browsers never cause these

tls-abort.name: TLS handshake aborted
tls-abort.desc: Handshakes dropped, reset or timed out are banned after 20 times in 1 minute. Browser preconnects and unstable networks cause these too, so do not lower the count

tlsKindHelp.eof: The peer connects then closes, or drops mid-handshake. Common in port probes; browser preconnects also do this.
tlsKindHelp.reset: The peer reset the connection (connection reset, broken pipe).
tlsKindHelp.timeout: The peer connects but never completes the handshake.
tlsKindHelp.protocol: The peer sends plain HTTP, SSLv2, garbage or a too-old protocol version. Normal browsers never do.
tlsKindHelp.negotiation: No shared cipher suite, key exchange, curve or application protocol.
tlsKindHelp.nocert: The requested domain belongs to no site (no certificate). A site with the domain filled in but no certificate is a configuration problem and is not counted.
tlsKindHelp.alert: The peer aborts with a TLS alert, e.g. it does not trust the certificate. Usually the client's own setup; not recommended for banning.
tlsKindHelp.other: Failures that fit none of the types above.
